steps.text: 7:00 A.M. \ Sunny, clear
Rhodes Island Dormitories
Mina? Mina? You up?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Nnuuh...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Shaky bedframe—bad...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Buh! You're already back, Kafka?

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: Just landed. Moseyed on down to you afore anything else... Oh, aaand I got a letter for you. From your dad.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Ooh, thanks!

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: You only got back yourself dead of night, didn'tcha?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Been takin' more stuff on these days...

steps.name: Kafka
steps.text: You hit snooze, then. I got a Logistics Dep to swing by.
Doing well, Mina?
Your mom wanted Kafka to run you some clothes, but I intervened. Figured your friend was plenty busy enough back here in Columbia, seemed it'd inconvenience her.
How's your new job? They call it Rhodes Island? Kafka says you get along just swell with your coworkers.
If both her and the old Simon Co. head are working there, I bet it must be rock solid.
8:00 A.M. \ Sunny, clear
Rhodes Island Engineering Department Hallway

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: ...Bridge's facade repairs are basically done. Just a little testing an' work's wrapped up all tidy. I—I'll get to it in a bit.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Heck, you're done two whole days ahead of schedule.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Best not forget to inspect the bridge this afternoon, Mr. Jeff.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: It's fine, when have you ever messed up on the job? I'm a proud mentor here.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: Say, Pinecone, were you in a hurry to get out this morning?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh... don't think so.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: Look at your socks. One's a stocking and the other's ankle-high. Not to mention the color clash.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh, shoot!

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Looks like you got muddled again. Maybe that afternoon inspection really is called for.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh, socks are socks, work's work...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: You don't slip up at work either, but last week, um, you had your gloves in the microwave like they were a loaf of bread.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: Yeah, you sure did! And Closure chewed you out hard for that.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Look, I was half-asleep by that point, okay?

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Ahem... Okay, Pinecone, brass tacks. Here's the Engineering itinerary for today. Take it and get to work.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: I'll see you cafeteria-side at noon, Pinecone! Don't forget lunch this time!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mm-hm, got it.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: How long's she been here at Rhodes now?

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Clocking in close to a year. I was the one taking her through sign-on the day she reported in.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Registered her info, checked in at the dorms, and gave a tour of the landship. She was both curious and nervous the whole way. Didn't ask much, though, kept shy.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: But the very last step, the simplest one, that was a real wringer.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: The Engineering Operator contract's only a couple pages, right? She went through at least seven, eight times, checked over every single line with an HR op for any breach of contract clauses that might be lurking.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: HR was convinced she was straight-up a spy from some other firm...

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: And she was way too serious about work while she was new. Enough to make even Closure not wanna assign anything to her.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Less serious, and more terrified of messing up. She took everything real carefully. I hear it's 'cause of some stuff she went through in Columbia, Kafka mentioned it once.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: I remember nobody was willing to even crack a joke in front of her. Look at her now, though, firing your goofs right back at you.

steps.name: Engineering Operator B
steps.text: Hahahahah—sorry, Jeff, I just can't help it.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Quit giggling... we're on the clock.
Your dad's recovering just fine. The whole project's been put on hold, though, and even the office shuttered. I asked around, and heard it was an investor that went belly-up. Simon Co.?
I'd been stuck at home for half a year now, no new job to speak of. Really hanging over me, but what can you do?

That's just the line of work we're in. Doesn't matter if you're in the right, clashing with the site owner is a big no-no. People think you'll rock the boat. Not to mention Columbia's got construction workers to spare.

Thank heavens for all the money you've been sending home... It's all my fault for being so useless, Mina, I know I'm a burden on you. Dashing all over the place with Rhodes Island can't be easy going either.
1:00 P.M. \ Sunny, clear
Rhodes Island Convalescent Garden

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Thank you for taking the time today, Pinecone.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I found all these ruptured floor tiles yesterday while inspecting the greenhouse. Water's seeped all unevenly through the walls too.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Sprinklers are working alright?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm, PRTS upgraded them just last month.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh-huh... floor got a case of overworn moisture proofing...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Will it be hard to fix?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Add extra dried charcoal to each part's proofing, re-lay the proofing for the damaged floor tiles, and that should do it.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Not much hassle, but... it'll take a li'l bit. Just leave this to me.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Phew—this should be good...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: (Ungh—shoulders are killing me...)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: You've been at this for five hours straight, I can't thank you enough! I got you some flower cookies—take them, I insist.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Let me see you out.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: You got so many flowers here. Didn't even notice till now.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: We barely ever see you in the Convalescent Garden! How about I give you the tour? It's the perfect opportunity.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: We cultivate a lot of rare flora here. Miss Lena says you could compare it to an entire small-scale botanical garden.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: That's some mighty fine work...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I loved reading things like The Nomadic City Gazetteer, back in Bolívar.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: They wrote about how all the big cities had gardens and nature museums, and how they'd hold regular botanical expos, and that they'd assemble all kinds of rare plant life for people to admire.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: And I wanted to go and see those places for myself, so badly.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Did ya ever go, then?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I never did. Right after I left home, I met Miss Lena, and then I came to Rhodes Island with her.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: These are summer wisterias, these are iridescent hydrangeas...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: These are coralblack willows... These are skeleton flowers, a very mysterious kind. They're native to the Higashi mountains.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: You can see how they're pink right now, right? But when they get wet in the rain, they slowly turn translucent!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: They do?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm, it gave me such a shock the first time I saw it. Do you want to see, Pinecone? I could sprinkle a little water...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh—I'm good, I'm good.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: These are fire crotons... The ones in the pots over there are pinetails, which flower for just one short week.
Oh wilderness, wilderness, runnin' for the sky♪
Oh city home, city home, my palms they hold you right♪
Machines do roll, do roll with care♪
Say don't roll over them grassreed hairs♪
They'll move to city home, come some right time♪
They'll live with us, come some right time♪

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Hmm, hmm—uh, sorry 'bout that...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: No, that was wonderful! What's that song called?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Dad taught me it, um... it's just those lines, no name, really.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I used to... put in shifts with my dad at the site, but work was always on. Barely got to talk the whole day.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: So after we clocked out, he'd walk me home real relaxed-like. We sung that song all the time, to shake the day off.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Sing it the whole way, and suddenly you're not so tired anymore.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Did you help build a lot of new cities, while you were in Columbia?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: The lyrics talked about taking the plants home, so you must've had gardens and nature museums, right? So were there really flower expos?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Nnuuh...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I—I don't know... Dad came up with the words himself...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: All I really remember's the wilderness... A whole lotta heavy machinery driving out into the barrens, bringin' along all the workers and materials together.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Construction's awful loud, even scarin' off all the fowlbeasts living nearby. Nothin' but dust, all across the land and sky... 'n then layer after layer of buildings rising on up, fast as fast goes.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Sometimes the foreman'd tell us what the buildings were for. Office block, lab, observatory... 'n all together they'd form a city.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Um... but it wasn't like we could imagine how it'd pan out after folks moved in.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Once one project gets wrapped up, the machines all moved us off to a new patch of wild... Some folk who fell ill and couldn't work anymore got left where they were...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Altogether, I guess, um... we only ever saw the city blueprints, and the materials to build 'em, never the actual city.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh, that's far enough. If the seepage ain't sorted out, come get me anytime.
But surprise! Your dad's found new work!

Remember Uncle Peter? He's an old work buddy of mine, and now he's a foreman. Does right by his friends too, I tell you! Called me in to the site. Good thing I kept covering his shifts all those years ago!

We're working on a small-scale nomadic city right now. I hear it's going to be used to temporarily settle people forced to migrate. It's no real big place, but functional enough, and welfare facilities are all well accounted for.
Peter says they're anticipating this city to work like a burdenbeast, doing runs through the wilds between big places like Trimounts, taking in anyone without a homeland anymore.
And it's all up to us to see to it that this burdenbeast gallops smooth!

Never thought Peter was foreman material, to be honest. The way he talks has grown just as much too. But he sure tells it like it is. There's still a hell of a lot of meaning in us building these hulking new cities.
That's our lot as frontier workers. The men don't matter so much, but the things we do matter like nothing else.
Rhodes Island disused training grounds

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Umm... is she not here yet?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Whoof—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Late, sorry about that.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I—It's fine, I just got here from the Convalescent Garden.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: You've never been skateboarding, yeah? I copied a few photos from when I won 'Legs on Wings.' Check it, that's the skatepark behind me there.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I can—give it a shot.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I owe you, Pinecone. You're doing me a solid.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: It's fine. Closure says the landship needs more recreational facilities to help us all destress... but it might be kinda cramped indoors...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: A buffer zone, some grind rails, a quarter-pipe, a half-pipe, a bowl, and a wave... That's all you need to kick it. Watch me if you don't believe.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Lucky it's sloped right here. Hmmm... if we buff out the floor a little, then install a bar down here beside the...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: For sure. You do that, I can finally pull off that nosegrind. Sweet!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: What was, um, the 'Legs on Wings' thing you...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: It was this trick skateboarding competition a couple blocks got together to hold. Nothing big-time, but crazy professional. Champion's prize was a high-grade, custom-made board... yeah, see what I'm riding right now? This is one of them bad boys.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: They quit holding it even before I started getting treated at Rhodes, though.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Wh—Why?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Neighborhood was old bones, government turned it over to a megacorp to turn into a commercial sector. Said they were gonna build this business complex over the park we hung out at.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Whoops, I meant 'commercial sector.' All they did was the same shady business once they landed...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But in a city as big as Trimounts, skating, graffiti, it's stuff they only let you do in a designated area... a tiny little corner.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh. But isn't it meant to be... real neat stuff?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Neat's not a word to them, y'know? Freedom, risk... the bigshots don't like that stuff.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: They need order, doesn't matter if it's good or bad. 'Street culture's' just a dirty word to those guys.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I didn't... know that about cities...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Pshh... who cares, we got the last laugh. Sprayed dumb faces all over their construction site warnings...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mr. Jeff, what're you doin' here...? Di—Did somethin' turn up with the bridge maintenance?

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: That's been checked and green-lighted. But I'm sorry, we're probably gonna need to call a halt to your skatepark project.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Um. We already notified Closure about it beforehand.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Here's the thing, Pinecone. This training grounds was pegged for specialist combat drilling in the future. They're gonna overhaul the whole space to simulate battle environments.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Closure had to put it on the backburner, but now...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mr. Jeff, to be honest...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Aw, forget it, Pinecone. Skateboarding's the freest art anyway. What kinda Champion Legs on Wings would I be if I let a park tie me down?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But if people complain to Logistics about how 'somebody's making a racket skating in the halls,' that's not my problem, yeah?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: We taking these poles and stuff down now then?

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Good thing you'd only just started. Should be a cinch to return a place this small to the way it was.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Um, uh, do—don't take it down for now!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mr. Jeff, the, um—follow-up training ground refurb, could you—could you let me be in charge of that?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: To be honest, the pipes and bowls and wave ramps you need for trick skateboarding seem real close to how the terrain gets rugged in the countryside...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: You think there's the possibility, uh, the stunt track could be... integrated with the development of the training grounds?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Could you let me be in charge? I—I want Operator Aciddrop and the rest... to have a place they can skate freely.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: If I recall correctly, this is the first time you're proactively applying for a role, after all your time here at Rhodes.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: The refurb's a big project, though. If you want to blend it with a skatepark, I can't imagine it'll be all that easy. You'll need to learn a whole lot of things...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I—I can give it my best shot.

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Then you find Closure soon, and apply. I can be there to vouch for you.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Um... huh? Really? Thanks a dozen, Mr. Jeff!

steps.name: Engineering Operator A
steps.text: Alright, I'll see you then.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Why'd you hafta go and sign up for all that extra work? I'm feeling beat just thinking about it.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh, um, I don't really know either. I just felt, I should try as hard as I could...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Rhodes Island's—like a little city of its own, I s'pose... and cities ought to be real grand.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Grand? Now that's a loaded word.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mm. Billboards on all the sites in Columbia kept using it—'build grand new cities, beautify Columbia's badlands.'

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I asked my dad, once, just what a—a grand city was.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Though to be honest, he didn't know either. Still, I reckon it should be somewhere with everything... with botanical gardens and nature museums, regular plant life expos where everyone can come see the pretty flowers...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: And giant libraries you can read in, no matter who you are.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: And streets free for everyone to skate on, and walls so they can graffiti as much as they like...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Not to be a wet blanket, but every city in Columbia's gonna disappoint you with those standards.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: They use slogans to dupe the workers, and ideals to dupe the youth. That's Columbia.

spans.text: They use slogans to dupe the workers, and ideals to dupe the youth.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Er, um... you're right about that.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: But, well, but my dad told me, Columbia's got more pioneer workers than you can count. Probably hardly anyone reckons we matter, but the things we do have gotta matter a whole lot.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Uh. Us, ourselves, we ought to believe in that.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: He was real sick before. It took a lot before he got better. But recently he found his way back to work. Said he was building a grand new city too.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: So, I just think it's right I keep at it too...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: If nothing we built before amounted to any kind of grand city, then at least starting now, I can make Rhodes Island a better place.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Um. So first, we gotta get you somewhere you can skate freely.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Rad... I've got your back on this one!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And also, you take part in our 'Legs on Wings' competition too! In light of your outstanding contributions to the competition venue, we can seed you for the semifinals.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Mm... muh?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Well, we got a place now, so why not revive 'Legs on Wings' here while we're at it? You dig it, right? I know you do!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (It'll be easy to win over the Doc and Amiya anyways.)

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Umm, in—in that case, I'll go apply with Closure at Engineering tomorrow... so we can get your venue set up soon as we can.
Rhodes Island Dormitories

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Bridge, greenhouse, stunt park... That's everything for today, finally. Tomorrow, I gotta...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: ...It's some kinda late now. Mmm, I'm feelin' sleepy...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh, forgot about fixin' the loose bedframe. *yawn*—t'mmmorrow...
Oh wilderness, wilderness, runnin' for the sky♪
Oh city home, city home, my palms they hold you right♪
Machines do roll, do roll with care♪
Say don't roll over them grassreed hairs♪
They'll move to city home, come some right time♪
They'll live with us, come some right time♪
I'm on my way out to work now. Didn't think I'd have so much to write about. Didn't even get to anything important.
So I'll wrap this up quick, Mina. Work hard, and rest hard too. Take care of yourself.
